key_insight: Across both spin-coated and gravure-printed organic solar cells, performance loss during ageing is best explained by the mobility-lifetime product (μτ), not by lifetime alone.
engineering_relevance: For scalable OSC manufacturing, μτ provides a unifying degradation metric that connects processing-induced morphology changes to real device stability and efficiency loss.
method: Compared spin-coated and fully roll-to-roll-compatible gravure-printed PM6:Y12 solar cells.
Tracked devices under ~1000 h of continuous illumination.
Related performance decay to charge-carrier mobility, recombination lifetime, and morphology changes.
evidence_signal: The paper reports that PCE loss systematically follows μτ despite different initial device properties and degradation pathways, with printed devices showing increased lifetime but strongly reduced mobility.
watch_item: A longer recombination lifetime can be misleading; mobility loss, metastable recovery effects, and architecture-specific degradation must also be measured before extrapolating stability.
paper_title: Mobility-lifetime relation links photodegradation in spin-coated and gravure-printed organic solar cells
